newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae, GE in mortgage aid linkup.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae, GE in mortgage aid linkup.

text.p: The Federal National Mortgage Association on Monday announced a pilot plan under which it will expand loss mitigation efforts by streamlining the process of working with servicers to help homeowners with troubled mortgages.

GE Capital Mortgage Insurance Corp, a wholly owned subsidiary of GE Capital Services, itself a wholly-owned unit of General Electric Co, will authorize Fannie Mae to work with servicers to make and implement decisions on dealing with mortgages in delinquency or default, Fannie Mae said.

"GE Capital has agreed to outsource to Fannie Mae functions and decisions regarding repayment plans or other alternatives to foreclosure on loans that are in trouble," Michael Quinn, Fannie Mae senior vice president for loss mitigation, said in a statement.

The plan, to begin immediately, will be targeted to 15-20 lenders and servicers who will be invited by GE Capital to participate over the next few months. The program will focus on loans currently insured by GE Capital and owned by Fannie Mae, as well as some current production loans.

The program will include repayment over several months of late mortgage payments, modification of loan terms such as lowering interest rates, extending loan terms or capitalizing past due interest, and pre-foreclosure sales, in which a troubled borrower and Fannie Mae together sell the home.
